# R15 Condition/Qualification Preservation — TEST-PLAN.md (Fable advisory, refined; execution pending)

## Provenance
Authored via the Claude.ai Max bridge (Fable 5.1) as advisory design. No research/extraction provider experiment, no API/OpenRouter route, no paid experiment, no implementation run. Earlier advisory text is retained as history; this file is the current plan.

## Purpose
Discriminate full preservation of supported conditions/qualifications from coherent-but-incomplete extraction, inversion, scope leakage, contradiction collapse and serialization clipping, in source-only semantic inventories. Representation is unspecified. Structural validity is never evidence of semantic completeness.

## Oracle tiers
- **Tier A — deterministic.** Runs only on authored fixtures whose expected atoms/operators/scopes carry an explicit, reviewed mapping from the implementation's representation to fixture atoms, and on known-bad outputs (regression shapes). Byte/hash checks apply to evidence spans and receipts only.
- **Tier B — advisory.** Paraphrase entailment, normative force, scope ambiguity, materiality of uncovered spans, adequacy of uncertainty notes. Needs AI/human review even where metadata automates a known inversion or loss. Unseen-source completeness is always Tier B.
- **Triage signals (neither tier's verdict).** Dangling punctuation, non-terminal fragments, trailing commas, empty strings, script-set differences. They queue a string for atom-level survival and advisory review; they are not semantic failures by themselves. No translation capability is required; a supported proper name or term in another script is acceptable when grounded.

## Outcome vocabulary (per fixture, per atom; never summed)
- PRESERVED — expected atoms, operators, scope targets, dimensions and references present, grounded, not inverted; contradictions and ambiguities carried explicitly.
- BOUNDED-FAIL — explicit failure under the implementation's declared capacity policy (inclusive/exclusive/sentinel; per-unit or whole-inventory). No partial salvage, clipping or repair.
- SILENT-LOSS — atom, operator, scope, dimension or reference absent or shortened with no failure signal.
- INVERTED — operator, polarity, scope, modality or comparator contradicts the fixture.
- COLLAPSED — a fixture-marked contradiction or ambiguity resolved to one reading without uncertainty.
- FABRICATED — content not grounded in fixture bytes (resolved missing section, filled timezone, inferred status).
- NOT-EXPOSED / POLICY-UNDECLARED — bound or capacity policy not declared; recorded, not scored.

## Boundary rule
For each declared bound B, probe B-1, B, B+1 and interpret results by the declared inclusive/exclusive/sentinel policy. Exactly-B passing is not assumed. Global request/inventory limits may fail as whole-inventory BOUNDED-FAIL without naming a unit; per-unit limits should name the unit only if the implementation declares per-unit semantics. Local byte/char/token estimates are not matched-tokenizer or live-fit guarantees.

## Reference rule
A reference to content not in the supplied excerpt is UNAVAILABLE-IN-EXCERPT. That is not a jurisdictional/external legal classification. Unavailable references retain their target identifier and are not resolved. An invalid internal link is an inventory ID that points to no inventory node; it is a structural defect, distinct from an unavailable source reference. Waiver interaction with an unavailable requirement is UNKNOWN, not asserted either way.

## Test families (12)
| ID | Family | Fixtures | Tier A (automatic) | Tier B (advisory) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TF-01 | Full vs coherent-but-incomplete conjunction | FX-A, FX-A2 | atom coverage; grammatical-prefix detection | paraphrase adequacy |
| TF-02 | Boolean/operator inversion | FX-B, FX-A | operator per group; nesting shape | alternate encodings |
| TF-03 | Baseline vs granted-waiver scope; nested exceptions | FX-A2, FX-B, FX-E | waiver trigger ≠ offer; waived-set equality | scope paraphrase |
| TF-04 | Unavailable references vs invalid internal links | FX-B, FX-G, FX-S2 | unavailable marker + identifier; no resolution text; dangling-ID detection | reference-class choice where ambiguous |
| TF-05 | Modal strength, bare imperative, contradiction | FX-C | label within allowed set; both statements present | justification of chosen force |
| TF-06 | Proposed vs current status scope | FX-C, FX-C2 | status within allowed set per duty | scope-uncertainty wording |
| TF-07 | Independent clock/date/tz/receipt dimensions | FX-D | per-dimension equality incl. ABSENT | added-inference labeling |
| TF-08 | Unicode exact evidence and receipts | FX-F | evidence/receipt byte equality; no NFC collapse; declared offset unit; separator retention | paraphrase grounding |
| TF-09 | Capacity bounds and payload growth | FX-L | outcome consistent with declared policy; no clipped strings; growth table | growth acceptability |
| TF-10 | Receipts, coverage, truncation/receipt drift | FX-R, FX-A trunc | hash equality; span bounds; atom disappearance matches deletion | uncovered-span materiality |
| TF-11 | Member-scoped permissions, exception leakage | FX-E | member×condition×exception matrix | sufficiency vs necessity labels |
| TF-12 | Structure-only validity and regression string shapes | FX-S1, FX-REG | cycle/dangling/duplicate detection; triage flags; atom survival | whether a flagged string was the only carrier |

## Execution notes (Codex, later)
- `python -I`; fixtures in their own directory; scripts elsewhere; fixture bytes canonical.
- Fixture files keep `source` (bytes) separate from `expected` (checker data). No test instructions inside `source`.
- Contradiction variants require both statements plus uncertainty; coherent scope-change variants edit every conflicting sentence and require the new scope.

FX-REG.change: Downgrade string-health flags to triage signals; no forced translation; proper names in other scripts allowed.

expected_checker_behaviour_replacement.triage: Each of the five planted strings is queued (dangling terminator, non-terminal fragment, script outside source script set, trailing comma, empty). Queueing is not a verdict.
expected_checker_behaviour_replacement.atom_survival: For each queued string, map to its atom (A3, A5) via the reviewed mapping and report SURVIVES-ELSEWHERE vs ONLY-CARRIER-AFFECTED. Absence is judged per atom.
expected_checker_behaviour_replacement.script_rule: A string in a script not present in the source is a triage signal only. If it is a grounded proper name, term, or a marked translation/paraphrase pointing to a source span, it is not a failure. The checker must not require translation capability.
expected_checker_behaviour_replacement.punctuation_rule: Trailing comma / dangling conjunction is a triage signal; the string is then compared to its grounded span for prefix-truncation (Tier A) and adequacy (Tier B).

variant_added.expect: Queued by script signal, cleared as grounded proper name. Tier A grounding.

FX-L.change: Follow declared capacity policy; no exactly-B pass assumption; no unit-naming requirement for global limits.

expected_replacement.policy_first: Before scoring, record the implementation's declared policy per bound: inclusive/exclusive/sentinel; per-unit vs whole-inventory; failure signal shape. If undeclared, record POLICY-UNDECLARED and run probes descriptively.
expected_replacement.at_B-1_B_B+1: Acceptable outcomes at each probe are PRESERVED or BOUNDED-FAIL consistent with the declared policy. Whether exactly-B passes is determined by the declared inclusive/exclusive rule, not assumed.
expected_replacement.global_limits: For request/inventory-wide limits, an explicit whole-inventory BOUNDED-FAIL is acceptable without naming a unit. Unit-named failure is expected only where the implementation declares per-unit limits.
never_acceptable: partial salvage of an inventory presented as complete
false completeness markers after a limit hit
expected_replacement.payload_growth: report output bytes / source bytes per probe; growth is recorded, not scored; a cliff near a bound is a Tier B note
expected_replacement.token_caveat: local byte/char/token estimates are not matched-tokenizer or live output-fit guarantees

variants_replacement.expect: NOT-EXPOSED / POLICY-UNDECLARED; escalating offline probes (1k/4k/16k/64k bytes) recorded descriptively; any clipped string is still a failure.

oracle_limits: Tier A automation of operator/atom truth matrices applies only to authored logical fixtures (FX-A, FX-A2, FX-B, FX-C/C2 operators and comparators, FX-D dimensions, FX-E matrix, FX-G/S2 reference classes) and to known-bad output shapes (FX-REG), and only after an explicit reviewed mapping from the implementation's representation to fixture atoms exists. Without that mapping the fixture is run descriptively.
Byte/hash equality is an oracle for evidence spans and receipts only. Accurate grounded paraphrases are not required to be byte-identical; their adequacy is Tier B.

Generic paraphrase entailment, normative force of bare imperatives, status-scope reach of an opening phrase, waiver-trigger readings in FX-A, and materiality of uncovered spans are advisory and need AI/human review.

Script-set differences, trailing punctuation, fragments and empty strings are triage signals that route a string to atom-survival and advisory review; they are not universal semantic failures. No translation capability is required; supported proper names in other scripts are accepted when grounded.
Contradiction and ambiguity fixtures are scored on presence of both statements plus an uncertainty marker; the wording or form of that marker is advisory.
Capacity probes are interpreted only under the implementation's declared policy; absence of a declaration yields POLICY-UNDECLARED, not pass or fail.
Unavailable references are judged on identifier retention and non-resolution; the checker does not and cannot determine legal/jurisdictional status of missing sections.
No aggregate score, accuracy denominator or model performance claim is produced; all verdicts are per fixture, per atom.
Unseen-source (Tier B discovery) completeness is never automated by this plan.
unresolved_implementation_choices: Representation of qualifications (quoted span, paraphrase, logical form, graph, baseline/waived state pairs) and the reviewed mapping to fixture atoms.
Declared capacity policy per bound: which bounds exist, inclusive/exclusive/sentinel, per-unit vs whole-inventory, failure signal shape.
Offset unit (byte/codepoint/UTF-16) and receipt hash algorithm; whether receipts hash pre- or post-chunking bytes.
How contradictions, ambiguity (bare imperative force, status scope, waiver trigger) and unavailable references are expressed — presence is automatic, form is advisory.
Whether shared conditions and shared unavailable targets are linked many-to-many or duplicated per referrer; link-set equality is what is checked.
Whether a merged unit (e.g., A1+A2) counts as preserving both atoms — default accept if both are recoverable from the grounded span, otherwise advisory.
Whether 'proposed' status is per-assertion or document-level in the implementation; both accepted if each duty's allowed status set is satisfied.
Reviewer selection for Tier B (AI on the Claude.ai Max bridge vs human); requires separate authorization and is out of scope here.
